title: Halo Was a Mac Game First: Steve Jobs Revealed It in 1999
hook: Steve Jobs introduced Halo on stage at Macworld in 1999, back when it was a Mac game that began as a strategy title. Would it be a legend today if it had never moved to Xbox?
script: Did you know Halo was first revealed by Steve Jobs as a Mac game? Back in July of nineteen ninety nine, Bungie walked onto the stage at the Macworld Expo to show it off. Jobs introduced the demo himself, and Bungie's Jason Jones showed it running on a Mac. Halo was not a first person shooter back then. It started out as a real time strategy game built on Bungie's Myth engine. By the Macworld demo it had become a third person action game. It was headed for Mac and PC, not consoles. Then everything changed in June of two thousand, when Microsoft announced it was buying Bungie and its new game. Halo moved to the Xbox and became a first person shooter. It launched as the original Xbox's big day one game, almost exactly twenty five years ago this week. Mac players finally got their own version of the game in two thousand three, four years after that first demo. This week Xbox turned twenty five, and Halo Studios announced Firefight is coming to Halo: Campaign Evolved as a free winter update. So the game Apple fans saw first is still getting new content a quarter century later. Would Halo have been as big if it had stayed on the Mac? Follow for more gaming history.
